# Browser engine components

The Desktop Mode browser keeps the existing per-app WASM module for HTML parsing, layout output, and its narrow host API. It vendors Lexbor 2.3.0 for HTML5 DOM parsing and CSS selector/cascade processing. Duktape 2.7.0 is compiled into the native host as a per-browser JavaScript context because wasm3 does not implement the Emscripten setjmp/longjmp imports emitted when Duktape is compiled to guest WASM. Browser WASM calls have a thirty-two-million-instruction ceiling to accommodate complex real pages while remaining bounded; other apps retain the one-million-instruction ceiling. Font Awesome icon-font stylesheets are skipped before download because this renderer cannot use their downloaded font glyphs; other external stylesheets remain subject to the 512 KiB combined CSS cap. If a call still traps, its operation and runtime error are shown in the failed app window.

The browser retains up to 128 image resources and retrieves each document and image resource up to 8 MiB, resolves up to eight linked or CSS-imported stylesheets and external scripts, and recognizes lazy-loaded image attributes (`data-src`, `data-lazy-src`, and `data-original`). The final URL after redirects is the default document base; the first valid `<base href>` overrides it for relative stylesheets, scripts, images, links, and forms. Combined external CSS is capped at 512 KiB; each external script can be up to 256 KiB. For `<picture>`, it checks preceding `<source>` elements in order, matches their media query to the Vita viewport, accepts PNG/JPEG/WebP MIME types, and chooses a `srcset` candidate before falling back to the enclosed `<img>`; for ordinary `<img>`, it chooses a `srcset` width or density candidate based on the rendered target width, then falls back to `src`. Up to 128 CSS background-image/gradient rules are retained per document; matching background rules use selector specificity, then source order, to choose the winning image. Base64 `data:` image URLs for PNG, JPEG, and WebP are decoded locally for `<img>` and CSS `background-image` rules. Relative URL paths normalize `.` and `..` while preserving trailing slashes; CSS image URLs resolve against their stylesheet's final URL. PNG and JPEG use Vita2D's decoders; WebP is decoded with the VitaSDK libwebp build. Image downloads are signature-checked before they are cached. Lexbor parses HTML and CSS rules; document-root custom properties declared on `:root` or `html` are substituted in inline and external stylesheets, including `var()` fallbacks (full scoped custom-property cascade is not implemented). The Vita renderer applies inherited and inline text colors and backgrounds, plus CSS font sizing, quantized `line-height` spacing on explicit and wrapped text lines (rounded up to 19-pixel row steps), bold font weight, underline and strike-through decorations, uppercase/lowercase text transforms, and basic ordered/unordered lists (including hex, named, `rgb()` and `rgba()` colors), hidden elements, basic `display:block` and `display:inline` overrides, interpolated 25-band backgrounds for inline and stylesheet `linear-gradient()` values (including transparent stops and diagonal direction approximation), and a 25-band horizontal center-to-edge approximation for inline and stylesheet `radial-gradient()` values (not a two-dimensional radial field), and a coarse text flow for direct children of flex/grid containers (`flex-direction: column` places items on separate rows; CSS `gap`/`row-gap` add vertical rows and `gap`/`column-gap` add measured spaces; CSS alignment, track sizing, and item geometry are not applied), pixel and percentage image dimensions, vertical `margin`, `margin-top`, and `margin-bottom` spacing rounded to renderer rows, and vertical `padding`, `padding-top`, and `padding-bottom` rows filled with the block background (horizontal padding indents block text and reduces wrap width approximately; it does not implement a complete CSS box tree, and margin collapsing remains unsupported), and stylesheet and inline-style CSS background images, including base64 `data:` images. Image flow reserves vertical space from declared dimensions, then reflows following text and controls to the decoded image's intrinsic or constrained size; undersized reservations expand, oversized reservations contract, and CSS background images do not affect document flow. Images larger than the available page width are scaled proportionally, while tall images use the page's vertical scrollbar. Normal text wraps using the native font's measured pixel width, while `<pre>` preserves spacing and can overflow horizontally. Up to 32 form controls are retained per page. Text inputs, password fields, textareas, select menus, checkboxes, radio buttons, submit buttons, and non-submitting `type=button` controls are supported; CSS `width` affects the rendered width and hit area of fields, select menus, textareas, and buttons. Forms submit GET and URL-encoded POST data, URL-encoding successful named controls in document order (including non-ASCII bytes), with up to 8 KiB of encoded fields; GET parameters are inserted before any URL fragment. Passwords are masked on screen. Select options can be changed with a click, and textareas open the text-entry prompt. Required controls block submission while empty, and non-empty email fields must have a basic valid address shape; checkbox/radio state is interactive, unchecked controls are omitted, radio selection is exclusive within its form/name group, and disabled controls are omitted. Interactive vertical and horizontal scrollbars handle overflowing pages.

Inline and external classic JavaScript (`text/javascript`, `application/javascript`, `text/ecmascript`, `application/ecmascript`, and `application/x-javascript`, optionally with MIME parameters) execute in a per-browser Duktape context with a 2 MiB heap cap and an instruction budget. JSON-LD, module scripts, and other non-JavaScript script types are skipped and are not downloaded as executable resources. `document.write()` output is parsed as an HTML fragment and passed through the same renderer, so generated text, images, forms, and style blocks can appear in the page. The DOM subset exposes `document.body` and `document.documentElement`, plus `createElement()`, `createTextNode()`, and `appendChild()` for generated markup, plus `remove()` and `removeChild()` for ID-bearing elements; created nodes expose `nodeType`, `nodeName`, `tagName`, and `classList`, and support basic attributes, text, nested children, and ID-based `addEventListener()` for click/input/change/submit events; existing elements in the bounded DOM snapshot use internal element keys, so their event listeners also work when the markup has no `id`; it also supports `getElementById()`, `querySelector()`, `querySelectorAll()`, `getElementsByClassName()`, and `getElementsByTagName()` with tag, class, ID, attribute-existence and attribute-value operators (`=`, `~=`, `|=`, `^=`, `$=`, `*=`), descendant, direct-child, and `:checked`, `:disabled`, `:required`, `:not()`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:only-child`, `:empty`, `:root`, and numeric/odd/even `:nth-child()` selectors. Each script receives a snapshot of up to 256 DOM elements and 12 attributes per element, including boolean attributes such as `checked`, `disabled`, and `required`; existing elements expose a small mutable `style` object (`display`, `visibility`, `color`, `backgroundColor`, `fontSize`, `setProperty`, and `removeProperty`) that writes back through the DOM mutation bridge, and a session-only in-memory `localStorage` subset supports `getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`, `clear`, `key`, and `length`; text fields are bounded and truncated only at complete UTF-8 character boundaries. Handles expose `parentElement`, `parentNode`, `children`, and `closest()`, as well as `textContent`, `innerText`, `className`, `classList` (`contains`, `add`, `remove`, `toggle`), `innerHTML` (serialized child markup, capped at 383 bytes per element), `id`, `value`, `checked`, `disabled`, `getAttribute()`, and `matches()`. They accept writes to `textContent`, `innerText`, `innerHTML`, `className`, `id`, and `value`, plus `setAttribute()`, `removeAttribute()`, and `insertAdjacentHTML()` for `beforeend` and `afterbegin`; changes are applied to the Lexbor document before rendering, so inserted markup retains its attributes and page CSS. Button and submit-input inline `onclick` handlers execute in the isolated Duktape context and can mutate the current DOM; ID-bearing buttons and links support `addEventListener("click", handler)`; ID-bearing text fields support `addEventListener("input", handler)`; select option changes and checkbox/radio state changes support `addEventListener("change", handler)` with the updated control value and state; identified forms dispatch `submit` before native GET/POST navigation; `document` and `window` support `DOMContentLoaded`, `readystatechange`, and `load` listeners in document order and expose `document.readyState`; submit handlers can call `event.preventDefault()` to cancel submission. Link handlers can call `event.preventDefault()` to cancel navigation. Page initialization scripts are not re-run for clicks. `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, and `clearInterval` run against browser-window ticks, with at most 16 callbacks per tick. Event dispatch covers button and link clicks, text-field input, and checkbox changes, and bubbles supported events through snapshot-backed ancestors to document listeners; other event types and general JavaScript-initiated networking are not available. `location.href` is readable and writable, and `location.assign()` and `location.replace()` navigate through the browser request layer. Read-only URL fields expose protocol, host, hostname, port, origin, pathname, search, and hash; `document.URL`, `document.documentURI`, `document.baseURI`, and `document.title` expose the current navigation and parsed document metadata. Scripts do not receive filesystem or native OS bindings. Scripts inside generated fragments are not executed. Script exceptions and timeouts are isolated and skipped without inserting diagnostic text into the page.

This is a constrained Vita renderer, not a full desktop browser engine. Text still flows into rows rather than a complete CSS box tree. It applies text alignment to lines that fit the viewport. GET and URL-encoded POST forms submit successful named controls in document order, including the activated submit button; hidden fields are included without being drawn, unchecked checkbox/radio controls and disabled fields are omitted. General CSS geometry, fonts, true flex/grid layout, full DOM/event APIs, multipart forms, SVG, WebGL, and current browser standards are not implemented. Quark remains in the workbench as the supplied reference project; its own SDL window/event loop prevents linking it directly into the Desktop Mode window. The native decoder uses libwebp under its BSD-3-Clause license; the full notice is shipped in `native/licenses/libwebp-BSD-3-Clause.txt` and included in the VPK.

The Duktape configuration enables its execution interrupt callback. `BrowserJsHeap` supplies a capped allocator, and the browser host exposes no privileged functions to JavaScript.

`sh scripts/test-media-decoder.sh` runs the production WebP loading path on the host with a Vita2D texture stub. It checks decoded RGBA pixels, malformed input rejection, and texture cleanup. `sh scripts/test-wasm-app-runtime.sh` exercises the browser's image URL selection, downloads, cache writes, and draw calls with host mocks, plus root CSS custom properties and fallback values, a 700 KiB HTML document fixture to detect regressions to the former 512 KiB page limit; actual Vita rendering still needs a console or emulator run.

- Lexbor: Apache-2.0, `lexbor/LICENSE` and `native/licenses/lexbor-Apache-2.0.txt`.
- Duktape: MIT, `duktape/LICENSE.txt` and `native/licenses/duktape-MIT.txt`.
- Quark: Apache-2.0, `quark/LICENSE-2.0.txt`; source and API reference remain in this workbench.
